deities: Nagnechi Mata (form of Durga/Adi Shakti; Kuldevi of the Rathore Rajputs; at the main Nagana temple she is 18-armed Mahishasuramardini with the falcon/eagle symbol)
festivals: Dussehra (main celebrations documented at the principal Nagana temple - verify whether the Nagaur-district shrine holds these)

history.dynasty: Rathore (Marwar) tradition - the goddess is the Kuldevi of the Rathore Rajputs of Marwar and Bikaner
history.period: 13th-14th century origin of the cult at Nagana; age of the Nagaur-district shrine is unverified
history.summary: Identity flag: the famous principal temple of Nagnechi Mata is at Nagana village (Bikaner/Jodhpur/Barmer border region - sources differ on district), the Rathore clan goddess's main shrine established by Rao Dhuhad (grandson of Rao Siha, founder of Marwar), who brought the Chakreshwari idol from Kannauj between 1295-1305 (Vikram Samvat 1349-1366) and installed it at Nagana, where the name evolved from 'Nagana-chi' (of Nagana). The CSV town 'Nagaur' points instead to a much smaller local shrine - a 'Nagnechi Mata Mandir' is listed at Mandukara, Nagaur district (PIN 341319), and the geocoder matches a 'Nagnechi Mata Ji Temple' in Merta Sub-District, Nagaur district (PIN 341513), used here. No substantive history, festival or timing sources exist for the Nagaur-district shrine itself - the history above is the deity's documented history (verify against the master CSV whether the famous Nagana temple or this local shrine was intended). Coordinates are the geocoder's Merta sub-district pin and are approximate (verify).

town_description: Nagaur is one of Rajasthan's oldest cities - 'the cattle capital of India' - known for the Nagaur Fort (Ahhichatragarh), the Tarkeen Dargah and its January-February cattle fair; the district around it is a mix of desert towns, villages and local shrines.
